title: Add synthetic token shadow traces and alert attenuator
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a low-risk way to exercise token-level cost/latency signal paths end-to-end and to automatically calibrate alert thresholds for long-tail token behaviour without replaying real customer traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight synthetic trace generator ("shadow traces") and an alert attenuation component that uses shadow signal statistics to suggest quiet-window adjustments and throttle noisy alert bursts.

What this changes (high level):
- new service: observability/shadow-trace-proxy - generates and forwards synthetic token-level traces with provenance tags (synthetic=true, provenance=shadow).
- telemetry/schema: token_v2 fields added (token_energy_mj, token_phase, synthetic_provenance).
- dashboards: Shadow Trace Heatmap + Shadow/Real comparative sparklines, added to observability/dashboards/heatmaps.
- alerts: quiet_window_tuner rule and alert-attenuator config to gate alerting during predictable transient bursts derived from synthetic signals.
- SDK instrumentation: lightweight trace enrichment helper and opt-in switch for emitting synthetic markers in test harnesses.
- tests: e2e replay & stability tests that validate the full ingest -> enrichment -> alerting flow using shadow traces.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear: ENG-1283) [x] unit tests for schema and enrichment [x] e2e scenario to validate alert dampening [x] observability runbook addition [x] docs update (observability/shadow-trace-runbook.md)

Design notes: Shadow traces are intentionally low-cardinality and tagged so downstream sampling and billing logic can ignore them. They mirror real invocation shape distributions (prompt length, generation length, token-phase labels) but use randomized payloads and synthetic tenant ids. The alert attenuator computes a short-term adjustment factor for alert thresholds based on the ratio of shadow-derived burstiness to historical baselines; it never mutates SLOs, only suggestion/temporary quiet windows that can be surfaced in the UI.

Commit summary: commit 1: add shadow-trace-proxy skeleton + dockerfile, commit 2: telemetry schema updates and migration helpers, commit 3: dashboard jsonnet and test fixtures, commit 4: quiet_window_tuner implementation + policy, commit 5: SDK trace enrichment helper + docs and runbook, commit 6: e2e tests and CI pipeline updates.

Files changed (high level): 
- observability/services/shadow-trace-proxy/main.go
- observability/services/shadow-trace-proxy/Dockerfile
- telemetry/schema/token_schema_v2.yaml
- telemetry/migrations/2025-11-shdw-token-schema.sql
- dashboards/shadow_trace_heatmap.jsonnet
- alerts/quiet_window_tuner.yaml
- observability/alerting/attenuator_policy.go
- sdk/instrumentation/trace_enricher.go
- tests/e2e/shadow_trace_replay_test.go
- docs/observability/shadow-trace-runbook.md

Testing: Local unit tests for schema + enrichment run quickly (go test ./...), e2e run in CI uses the shadow-trace-proxy container and the staging observability stack. I validated: shadow traces ingest, enrichment attaches expected fields, dashboard panels render synthetic/real overlays, quiet-window-tuner suggests a 30s dampening window when synthetic burst ratio > 2x baseline, and the attenuator suppresses alert fanout for non-critical routes.

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind feature flag obs.shadow_traces.enabled=false. Staged enablement: enable in staging for 48h with monitoring of attenuator decisions, then opt-in for internal teams, then opt-in for selected customers. Manual kill-switch available in console and an automated rollback trigger if CI/live error rate > 0.1% in the first 1h after enable.

Operational runbook items added to docs/observability/shadow-trace-runbook.md: how to seed distributions, how to interpret heatmap overlays, how to revert attenuator suggestions, and an FAQ for security & billing (synthetic traces excluded from billing pipelines).

Security & privacy: Synthetic traces are generated with pseudo-IDs and TTL'd keys. No real prompt content is ever recorded or forwarded. The schema includes explicit downstream tagging so audit pipelines filter synthetic traces.

Related: ENG-1283 (design), ENG-2210 (alerting follow-up). Links: Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1283; runbook: docs/observability/shadow-trace-runbook.md

release_notes: Add synthetic shadow traces for safe observability testing and an alert attenuator that suggests quiet windows based on synthetic-derived burst patterns. Feature gated behind obs.shadow_traces.enabled. Includes dashboards, schema updates, and e2e tests.
notes: This is intentionally conservative: synthetic signals are marked and filtered out of billing and production SLO calculations.
Feature flag gating and runbook entries are included; recommend 48h staging verification before enabling in production.
Follow-ups: ENG-2210 to expose attenuator suggestions in the Console UI and ENG-2255 to collect long-term synthetic baselines for seasonal calibration.
